title: facebook
description: Scrapes posts, and optionally comments, from a public Facebook page or group. A date range is a window the run must COVER, not merely filter to: with start_date/end_date and no max_posts, the run collects every post in the range and reports whether it managed to cover it. Needs an authenticated session, forwarded to the Worker as FB_SESSION.

target.description: A page ('nasa', or a facebook.com/... URL) or a group ('groups/123456', a numeric group id, or a full group URL).

max_posts.description: Cap on posts returned. OMIT IT when using a date range: the range is then the stopping condition, and a count here would cut the window short.

start_date.description: Only posts at or after this moment (UTC, inclusive). A bare date means midnight.

end_date.description: Only posts at or before this moment (UTC, inclusive). A bare date means end of day.

collect_comments.description: Also collect each post's comments and replies. Considerably slower. Defaults to true.

max_comments_per_post.description: Cap on comments per post. Under a date range this counts comments written INSIDE the range.

comment_sort.description: Which comments a cap returns. 'relevant' is Facebook's own ranking and the default; 'newest' walks the connection in time order and is what a date range needs to cover a period rather than sample it.

page_concurrency.description: Split a dated PAGE scrape into that many concurrent date chunks. Ignored for groups, which have no server-side date seek and would just repeat the same walk.

analyse.description: Also produce an AI analysis and report (text, PDF and an HTML dashboard) alongside the data. Defaults to true. Costs two Claude calls; the scrape itself is unaffected either way.

ai_prompt.description: Your own analysis instructions, e.g. 'focus on complaints about delivery times'. Added to the built-in brief rather than replacing it, so the report keeps its structure and always renders.
